text: For the choirmaster. A psalm of the sons of Korah.
LORD, you showed favor to your land; you restored the fortunes of Jacob.
You took away the guilt of your people; you covered all their sin. Selah
You withdrew all your wrath; you turned from your burning anger.
Restore us, God of our salvation, and put away your indignation toward us.
Will you be angry with us forever? Will you prolong your anger through all generations?
Will you not revive us again, so that your people may rejoice in you?
Show us your steadfast love, LORD, and grant us your salvation.
Let me hear what God the LORD will speak, for he will speak peace to his people, to his faithful ones — but let them not turn back to folly.

versions.text: Let me hear what God the LORD will speak, for he speaks peace to his people, to his faithful ones — but let them not turn back to folly.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew imperfect יְדַבֵּר in the second clause parallels the first; rendering it as future keeps the parallel and matches the anticipatory tone of the verse.

text: Surely his salvation is near to those who fear him, that glory may dwell in our land.
Steadfast love and faithfulness have met; righteousness and peace have kissed.
Faithfulness springs up from the earth, and righteousness looks down from heaven.
The LORD himself will give what is good, and our land will yield its increase.

versions.text: The LORD himself will give what is good, and our land will yield its harvest.
versions.explanation: יְבוּל denotes the produce or yield of the ground generally, not specifically a harvest of grain; 'its increase' or 'its produce' is closer to the Hebrew.

text: Righteousness goes before him and makes a path for his steps.
